senses.gloss:
Dāva, ‘forest fire,’ is mentioned in the Atharvaveda^1 and
the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.^2 In the latter work such fires are
referred to as occurring in spring. According to Sieg,^3 a hymn
of the Rigveda^4 describes a forest fire. Watchers were
employed to guard against surprise from such conflagrations
(dāva-pa).^5
1) vii. 45, 2.
2) xi. 2, 7, 32.
3) Die Sagenstoffe des Ṛgveda, 44 et
seq.
4) x. 142. Sieg's interpretation of this
hymn is not at all probable.
5) Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxx. 16; Tait-
tirīya Brāhmaṇa, iii. 4, 11, 1.

Dāva-su Āṅgirasa, a seer of Sāmans, or chants, is mentioned
in the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa.^1
1) xxv. 5, 12, 14. Cf. Hillebrandt, Vedische Mythologie, 2, 160.
